title: Microsoft Purview: collection policies support in Insider Risk Management
summary: The roadmap facts, automatic policy creation, portal path and workload-based licensing are supported. The stronger statement that filtered activities cannot generate alerts is not explicitly documented, and some checklist controls have no corresponding table row. All six Learn links flagged by the pre-check opened successfully.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Insider Risk Management support for collection policies.
claims.quote: With this update, IRM will start supporting collection policies.

claims.claim: The change is on by default in the sense that required policies are created automatically for device-indicator IRM policies.
claims.quote: For device indicators based IRM policy, required collection policies will be automatically created in the background.

claims.claim: Collection policies filter which events are ingested into Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: They let you filter which events from both untrusted and trusted sources are ingested into Purview.

claims.claim: Ingested collection-policy data can be used by Insider Risk Management and Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Once ingested, that data can be classified and used by various Microsoft Purview signal consuming solutions, such as Microsoft Purview Activity explorer, Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management

claims.claim: An event includes a condition, such as content containing a sensitive information type.
claims.quote: For example, a condition could be Content contains a sensitive information type, like U.S. Social Security Number

claims.claim: An event also includes an activity, such as copying a file to removable media.
claims.quote: An activity that a user can take on a sensitive item, like File copied to removable media

claims.claim: Learn already documents device indicators as included in collection-policy evaluations, unlike the roadmap's future-tense support description.
claims.quote: Device indicators are included in collection policy evaluations.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A deployed device collection policy takes precedence over a conflicting IRM policy for device indicators.
claims.quote: the collection policy configuration takes precedence. This means that if an Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor a specific activity, but the collection policy is configured to filter out that activity, the activity isn't collected

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A device activity filtered out by the collection policy is not collected or available for review in IRM.
claims.quote: the activity isn't collected and isn't available for review in Insider Risk Management. This only applies to device indicators in Insider Risk Management policies, and only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.claim: No alert can be raised on an activity filtered out by the collection policy.
claims.quote: Searched: collection policy filtered device activity no alert Insider Risk Management. Read collection-policies-solution-overview, insider-risk-management-settings-policy-indicators and policy-template search results; they state not collected or available for review, not the stronger alert guarantee.
claims.fix: Remove 'and no alert can be raised on it'; retain the documented statement that the activity is not collected and is unavailable for review.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Purview combines collection policies for a data source into a single policy at evaluation time.
claims.quote: during policy evaluation, Microsoft Purview combines all the collection policies for a data source into a single collection policy for that data source. So all the conditions for a data source are used when identifying matches.

claims.claim: A device collection policy can be scoped to all users and groups.
claims.quote:
For each data source, you can choose to scope by:

- All users and groups (default)

claims.claim: A device collection policy can be scoped to specific users and groups.
claims.quote:
For each data source, you can choose to scope by:

- All users and groups (default)
- Specific users and groups

claims.claim: A device collection policy can cover all users except specified users and groups.
claims.quote:
All except specific users and groups

Note

Excluded users and groups take precedence over any included users or groups.

claims.claim: With no conditions, a device collection policy detects all data, including data that does not match the organisation's classifiers.
claims.quote:
If you don't add conditions, what gets detected depends on the data sources you select later:

- Devices: All data is detected, even if it doesn't match your organization's classifiers.

claims.claim: Collection policies are tenant-level controls over the signals available to Purview solutions.
claims.quote: Collection policies are a configuration option in the Microsoft Purview portal that allows administrators to fine-tune what are the signals and data that are available to Purview solutions at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Collection policies are reached in the Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, select Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies.

claims.claim: Collection policies can also be accessed through Information Protection > Classifiers in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Alternately, you can access collection policies in the Microsoft Purview portal from Solutions > Information Protection > Classifiers > Collection policies.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation for creating or editing these collection policies is documented as of November 2026.

Read overview, deployment guide, Graph data-security overview; searched Exchange cmdlet index: no matching operation.
